title: The beginning of sorrow in Gethsemane
english: Taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be sorrowful and troubled (Matthew 26:37). These were the very disciples he took with him on the mountain when he was about to be transfigured (Matthew 17:1). He began to be sorrowful—there is a great difference between being sorrowful and beginning to be sorrowful. Tempted in every way according to likeness, apart from sin (Hebrews 4:15), he did not sorrow with the sorrow of the passion itself, but began to according to human nature.
translator_notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Matthew's account of Jesus taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee apart in Gethsemane, where he begins to be sorrowful and troubled.

title: The Father's will over the Son's human will
english: “Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; yet not as I will, but as you will” (Matthew 26:39). In taking up the nature of human flesh, he fulfilled all its properties, so that he would not be thought to have had flesh in appearance only, but in truth. It is proper to every faithful person first to refuse to suffer, especially to the point of death; but if God wills it, to acquiesce even against one's own will.
translator_notes: Series rem Gethsemane from PG 13 Latin.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane, explaining how his sorrow and reluctance belong to the true human nature he took on.
